==English==
{{wp}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈmɪks/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-mix.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɪks|s=1}}
* {{homophones|en|micks|Micks|Mick's}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{l|en|mixe}} {{qualifier|archaic}}

===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*meyḱ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|mixen}} (attested in past tense as {{m|enm|mixed}}, {{m|enm|myxyd}}), from {{inh|en|ang|[[*mixian]]}}, {{m|ang|[[miscian]]}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*miskijan}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*miskijan|t=to mix}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro||*miḱ-sḱé-ti}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*meyǵ-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*meyḱ-|t=to mix}}.

Cognate with {{cog|stq|miskje||to mix, blend}}, {{cog|dum|mischen||to mix}}, Low German {{m|nds-de|misken}}, {{m|nds-de|mischen||to mix}}, {{cog|goh|miskian}}, {{m|goh|miskēn||to mix}} ({{cog|de|mischen}}), {{cog|cy|mysgu||to mix}}, {{cog|la|misceō||mix}}, {{cog|grc|μῑ́γνῡμῐ||to mix}}, {{cog|cu|мѣсити||to mix}}, {{cog|lt|mišti}} and {{m|lt|maišyti||to mix}}, {{cog|sa|मिश्र||mixed}}, {{cog|fa|آمیختن|tr=âmixtan||to mix}}, {{cog|ang|māsc||mixture, mash}}.<ref>Skeat, ''An Etymological Dictionary of the English Language'', "Mix."</ref> More at [[mash]].

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[stir]] together.
#: {{ux|en|'''Mix''' the eggs and milk with the flour until the consistency is smooth.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|title=Dinner in One|author=Melissa Clark|year=2022|ISBN=9780593233252|page=
|text=In a medium bowl, '''mix''' together the leeks, lemon zest, the remaining ¼ teaspoon salt, and the remaining 1½ tablespoons oil.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[combine]] (items from two or more sources normally kept separate).
#: {{ux|en|to '''mix''' business with pleasure}}
#: {{ux|en|Don't '''mix''' the meat recipes with the dairy recipes.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 6-1|act=III|scene=iii|passage=What here shall '''miss''', our toil shall strive to mend.}}
# {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To form by mingling; to produce by the stirring together of ingredients; to concoct from different parts.
#: {{ux|en|Yellow and blue paint '''mix''' to make green.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Romeo and Juliet|act=III|scene=iii|passage=Hast thou no poison '''mixed'''?}}
#* {{RQ:Bacon Holy War|90|Therefore J haue chosen an Argument, '''mixt''' of ''Religious'' and ''Ciuill'' Considerations; And likewise '''mixt''' between ''Contemplatiue'', and ''Actiue''.}}
#* {{RQ:Boyle Cold|chapter=Title I. Experiments Touching Bodies Capable of Freezing Others.|paragraph=13|page=49|passage=In order to the diſcovery of ſome hints of the account, upon which the above mentioned mixtures were more intenſely frigefactive than ſnow alone, we ſealed up a ſingle vial of ſnow unmingled with any other ingredient, and found it to thaw much more ſlowly than any of thoſe parcels of ſnow, which we had '''mixt''' with ſalts or ſpirits.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[blend]] by the use of a [[mixer]] {{gloss|machine}}.
#: {{ux|en|'''Mix''' the egg whites until they are stiff.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|music}} To combine (several tracks).
#: {{ux|en|I'll '''mix''' the rhythm tracks down to a single track.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|music}} To produce a finished version of (a recording).
#: {{ux|en|I'm almost done '''mixing''' this song.}}
# {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To unite with in company; to join; to associate.
#* {{RQ:KJV|Hosea|7|8|passage=Ephraim, he hath '''mixed''' himself among the people.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1866|author=William Henderson|title=Notes on the Folk-lore of the Northern Counties of England and the Borders|page=183
|passage=The mention of the six knots of elderwood is curious, for that tree '''mixes''' largely in folk lore.}}

===Etymology 2===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*meyḱ-}}
A merger of a nominal use of the verb and a borrowing from {{der|en|xno|mixte}}, from {{der|en|la|mixtus}}, past participle of {{m|la|misceō||mix}}. Nowadays regarded automatically as the nominal form of the verb.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# The result of mixing two or more substances; a [[mixture]].
#: {{ux|en|Now add the raisins to the '''mix'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2015|author=Don E. Schultz; Beth E. Barnes; Heidi F. Schultz|title=Building Customer-brand Relationships|page=102
|passage={{...}} fifteen flavors of powdered '''mixes''' in traditional scoop-out packages, seven flavors of single-serve bottled drinks, and three flavors of multiserve bottles.}}
# The result of combining items normally kept separate.
#: {{ux|en|My recipe file was now a '''mix''' of meat and dairy.}}
#: {{ux|en|The combination of classical music and hip hop is a surprisingly good '''mix'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Time|title=As Colleges Open During a Pandemic, Student Life Remains Closed|author=Katie Reilly|date=Sept 10 2020|passage=A Chronicle of Higher Education tracker of nearly 3,000 colleges found that of those with firm plans, 19% are opening primarily in person; 27% are primarily online; and 16% are, like Penn State, a '''mix'''.|url=https://time.com/5887324/college-campus-coronavirus/|accessdate=11 September 2020|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200911233505/https://time.com/5887324/college-campus-coronavirus/|archivedate=11 September 2020}}
# A preparation, usually in the form of a powder, into which other ingredients can be mixed to prepare a specified foodstuff. 
#: {{ux|en|[[cake mix|Cake '''mix''']]. [[pancake|Pancake]] '''mix'''. [[hot chocolate|Hot chocolate]] '''mix'''.}}
# {{lb|en|music}} The result of mixing several tracks.
#: {{ux|en|The rhythm '''mix''' sounds muddy.}}
# {{lb|en|music}} The finished version of a recording.
#: {{ux|en|I've almost finished the '''mix''' for this song.}}
# {{lb|en|US|slang|uncountable}} A substance used to [[dilute]] or [[adulterate]] an [[illicit]] [[drug]].<ref>Tom Dalzell (ed.), ''The Routledge Dictionary of Modern American Slang and Unconventional English,'' New York: Routledge, 2009, p.{{nbsp}}665.</ref>
#: {{syn|en|[[cut#Noun|cut]]}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1977|author=John Allen|title=Assault with a Deadly Weapon: The Autobiography of a Street Criminal,|location=New York|publisher=Pantheon Books|chapter=11|page=160|url=https://archive.org/details/assaultwithdeadl00alle_0/page/160/mode/1up?q=mix
|passage=Eventually I could taste different drugs and tell how much '''mix''' in it or if there’s too much '''mix''' in it or what have you.}}
